newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil dominated by diesel trading.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil dominated by diesel trading.

text.p: Diesel dominated the NWE gas oil market on Tuesday with heating oil having to settle for the back seat.
Futures gave only modest support to outright prices with May IPE last trading only 25 cents up at $165.25 a tonne.
Traders said there was a lot of diesel business on Tuesday to build on a couple of deals done Monday. Premiums ranged by $2 a tonne, although there was some scepticism about some of the prices.
"I think the market is around +$11.50 to +$12.50 despite people hearing deals above and below this," said one trader.
A flexi cargo was understood sold at the high number of May IPE +$13.25 cif Le Havre which is about $1 above Monday's deal of May IPE +$14.50 basis Bordeaux.
"I think it's connected with a swaps position," said one trader citing another trade at May IPE +$12.25.
Two other cargoes were also heard done, one into Hamburg at May IPE +$9.50 prompt and another at May IPE +$11.25 cif France for first half May. The latter trade was seen cheap, by several traders.
FOD and DIN were attracting only modest talk of around May IPE +$3-4 cif NWE, but nothing was done.
